notes: Camera Border maker: right-click a camera (or anything in a scene) › Border… Round its corners or make it a circle, add a ring of colour (plain or a gradient) and a glow or drop shadow, and see it change live in the preview as you adjust it.
Six presets to start from: Clean white, Neon glow, Soft shadow, Circle, Gold frame and Thin and square.
Save as PNG writes the border with a clear inside to Pictures › NorthRay Capture, to use as an overlay anywhere.

Each streaming destination chooses its sound: the Stream mix, or one of the six recording tracks (Settings › Streaming › Sound). Destinations still share the video encode. Not yet tested on a live stream on Windows; please report how it goes.
A second output (Settings › Audio) plays any one mix on another device as well, such as a line out to a streaming PC.
Quick routing in a source's Send to menu: Stream and recordings, Recordings only, Stream only, or Only me.
The routing check warns if the second output would feed desktop audio back into itself, or shares the monitor's device.

Audio filters: right-click a sound source in the Audio mixer › Filters. Gain, noise gate, noise suppression, expander, compressor, limiter, equaliser, balance and delay, in the order you choose, each with its own switch and values.
Presets to start from: a microphone (clean and even), a game or music (kept in check), or a safety limiter.
Filters change the source's own sound before its volume and routing; its test clip records the result.

Video and sound files as a source (+ in Sources): one file or several played in turn, looping or shuffled if you like, with Pause, Play, From the start and Next in its menu. Its sound has its own channel in the Audio mixer.
Stinger transitions: a video plays over the switch and the scene changes at the moment you choose (Transition › Stinger).
Custom shader transitions: write your own in HLSL (Transition › Custom shader › Make an example file to start from). If it doesn't compile, the menu says why and a fade is used.
Groups: right-click a source › Group with to move, resize and hide several sources as one; Ungroup puts them back.
Not yet: web pages as sources.
Scene folders: right-click a scene › Folder to put it in a folder. The Scenes list shows each folder as a heading with its scenes under it.

Export a scene to a file, and import one (right-click a scene). The file holds the scene, any scenes shown inside it, and their sources and placements; it never holds stream keys. Images and other files are referred to where they are, not copied in.
An imported scene gets names that don't clash with yours, and its placements are resized if it was made for a different canvas size.

New sources (+ in Sources): an image (animated GIFs play, and the picture updates by itself when the file is changed), text, a colour, a slideshow of a folder's images, and part of the screen (drag a rectangle over a still of your desktop).
Text has its own settings in its menu: the words, font, size, colour, bold, italic, alignment, line wrapping, and an outline with its colour.
Every source's menu now has Position and size (type the numbers), Rotation, Opacity and Duplicate.
Images, text, colours and slideshows can be partly see-through; what's behind them shows.

Transitions: switching scenes can now cut, fade, slide, swipe or luma wipe. Choose it under Transition in Controls, with its duration (0.15 to 2 seconds) and easing, the direction for slides and swipes, and the pattern and edge for luma wipes. Recordings and streams show the transition too.

Studio Mode (Controls): the preview splits into Preview, where you prepare a scene without anyone seeing, and Program, what's live (red frame). Transition, or Ctrl+Enter, puts the preview live. The Scenes list marks the live scene, and the preview warns you when you're editing the scene that's live.
Scenes inside scenes: + in Sources › Scene shows another scene inside this one, like any other source (move it, resize it, crop it). Capture won't let a scene end up inside itself.
Not yet: stinger and custom shader transitions, and image, text and slideshow sources (next).

Multistreaming: stream to several places at once (up to six), straight from Capture, with no restreaming service. Add destinations in Settings › Streaming, each with its own service, server, stream key and bitrate.
Destinations at the same bitrate share one encode, so the video is encoded once; a destination at a different bitrate (say Twitch at 6 Mbit/s and YouTube at 8) gets its own.

Each destination has its own connection, buffer and reconnection: one dropping or failing never stops the others. In Controls, each has its own row (live time, bitrate, dropped frames, reconnections, or why it stopped); click a row to start or stop just that one.
Settings › Streaming shows the upload all the switched-on destinations need, and lets you choose the longest wait between reconnection attempts.
Your 0.6 streaming settings and stream key carry over as the first destination.
Signing in to Twitch and YouTube has been taken out again: stream keys are pasted in, per destination.

Please note: the destinations were tested here with four local test servers at once (stopping one, adding one, one reconnecting by itself). This computer has no H.264 or AAC encoders, so the shared encode and streaming to real platforms haven't been tried yet.

Sign in to Twitch or YouTube (Settings › Streaming › Account) and Capture gets your stream key itself each time you go live, and for YouTube the server too, so a key reset on the website is picked up.
Twitch: your browser opens Twitch's page with a code to approve; Capture shows the same code so you can check. YouTube: you sign in with Google in your browser.

Capture asks only to read the stream key (Twitch) or to read your YouTube account (YouTube): it can't post, change your channel or read your messages. Sign-ins are kept in Windows Credential Manager; Sign out removes them and cancels them with Twitch or Google.

Please note: signing in needs NorthRay Capture to be registered with Twitch and Google, which hasn't happened yet, so in this version the Account row says it isn't set up and the stream key is entered as before. The sign-in itself has been tested here against a stand-in for both services, not the real ones.
Streaming: Start streaming in Controls. Choose Twitch, YouTube, Kick or a custom server in Settings › Streaming, and enter your stream key.
The stream key is kept in Windows Credential Manager on this PC. It's never shown, and never written to settings or logs. A key pasted on the end of a server address is moved there too.
Secure streaming (RTMPS) uses Windows' own TLS, and Capture checks the server's certificate itself: a wrong name or an untrusted authority is refused, with the reason.

If the connection drops, Capture keeps going and reconnects by itself (after 2 seconds, then longer, up to a minute). A stream key the platform refuses isn't retried. If the network can't keep up, old frames are dropped rather than the stream falling behind, and counted in the status bar.
The status bar shows the stream's state, time, bitrate and dropped frames. Recording and streaming can run together.

Please note: streaming has been tested here against a local test server, over plain and secure connections. This computer has no H.264 or AAC encoders, so it hasn't yet run with a real encoder or to a real platform. If it doesn't work, the message and the log (Settings › Open the logs folder) say why.
Not yet: streaming to several platforms at once (next) and saving a recording as MP4.

Recording: Start recording in Controls. The canvas is encoded as H.264 by your graphics card's encoder where it has one (NVIDIA, AMD or Intel), or by Windows' software encoder, with the recording tracks chosen in Settings › Recording as AAC audio tracks, each named after the sources on it.

Recordings are MKV files in Videos\NorthRay Capture (or the folder you choose). They're written so that everything up to a crash or power cut still plays. Recording stops cleanly if the disk is nearly full.
Settings › Recording: the folder, the video encoder (automatic or a chosen one), video quality (6 to 40 Mbit/s), which audio tracks go in the file, and audio quality.
While recording: the time in Controls, and the time, the file's size and any lost frames in the status bar.
A sync test source (+ in Sources › Sync test): a white flash and a beep at the start of each second, for checking that picture and sound line up in a recording.

Please note: recording has only been tested here as far as the file format. This computer has no H.264 or AAC encoders, so recording hasn't yet run with a real encoder. If it doesn't work on your PC, the message and the log (Settings › Open the logs folder) say why.
Not yet: streaming (next) and saving a recording as MP4.

Audio routing: each sound source can be sent to the stream (what viewers hear), recording tracks 1 to 6, and the monitor (what you hear) independently, with the buttons under its fader or “Send to” in its right-click menu. A source that isn't sent to the stream is absent from it, not just turned down.
New sources start on the stream and track 1 (everything), plus a track of their own kind: microphones on 2, desktop audio on 3, programs on 4, ready for editing later.
Monitoring: the monitor mix plays on the device chosen in Settings › Audio (Windows' default to begin with). The mixer shows meters for the stream and the monitor.

Warnings in the mixer when a program kept off the stream would still reach viewers through desktop audio, when the same sound reaches a mix twice, when monitoring desktop audio would feed back into itself, and when a microphone could pick up monitoring played through speakers. A leak can be fixed in one click (on Windows 11): desktop audio leaves that program out.
Desktop audio can leave one program out (right-click › Leave a program out, Windows 11). Windows allows one program per desktop audio source.
Settings › Audio lists where each sound source goes, and any problems.
Save a 10-second test clip of the stream mix, any track or the monitor (right-click a sound source › Save a test clip of a mix).
The mixer scrolls with the mouse wheel when its sources don't all fit.

Sound capture: add a microphone or other input, desktop audio (everything an output device plays) or, on Windows 11, one program's sound on its own from + in the Audio mixer (or in Sources). A program is found by name, so its sound is captured again whenever it restarts; sources set to Windows' default device follow it when it changes.

The Audio mixer: a level meter for each sound source and for the mix (green, yellow and red, with a line at the recent peak), a volume fader showing decibels, and a mute button. Sound sources are heard in every scene.

Right-click a sound source to rename it, change its device or program, mute it, remove it, or save a 10-second test clip of just its own sound (before its volume and mute) to Videos\NorthRay Capture, so you can hear exactly what it captures.
Click a sound source's name to see its whole status, such as why a device can't be used.
Not yet: separate stream, recording and headphone mixes (next), recording and streaming.
Video capture: add a whole display, a window or a camera or capture card from + in Sources, and see it live in the preview.

Displays are captured with Desktop Duplication, or Windows Graphics Capture or a slower compatibility mode where that isn't available; you can choose the method and whether to show the mouse pointer from a source's right-click menu.

Windows are captured with Windows Graphics Capture (they can be covered by other windows). Capture remembers the program and finds its window again when it restarts; minimised windows keep their last picture.

Arrange sources on the preview: drag to move, drag the handles to resize (Shift for any shape), Alt+drag a handle to crop, with snapping to the edges and centre of the canvas (hold Ctrl to place freely). The arrow keys nudge (Shift for 10 pixels).

Each source's right-click menu: rename, hide, lock, fit to the canvas (Ctrl+F), stretch (Ctrl+S), centre (Ctrl+D), reset (Ctrl+R), rotate, flip, remove the crop, and order. The eye and lock buttons in Sources hide and lock.
A source can be shown in several scenes (“A source from another scene” under +) and is captured once.
The status bar shows how long the graphics card takes for each frame, and the preview shows the frame rate being kept.
Not yet: sound, recording and streaming.
First version, in early development: the foundation. It doesn't capture, record or stream yet.

The workspace: a preview area and Scenes, Sources, Audio mixer and Controls panels. Drag the dividers to resize, drag a panel's header (or right-click it) to move or hide it, and save, load or reset layouts from Layout in the top bar.
Scenes: add, rename, duplicate, reorder and delete, switch with Ctrl+1 to Ctrl+9 or the arrow keys; saved automatically.
Settings: theme, low-resource mode, preview and output frame rates, canvas size, the encoders found on your PC, the logs folder and Copy diagnostics.
Coming next: capturing displays, windows and cameras, with a live preview and moving and resizing sources on it.
